chunks: The Commander of the Faithful (may Allah's blessings be upon him) said: 'God Mighty and Majestic does not accept the supplication of a heedless heart.'

And Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whenever one of you supplicates for the deceased, he should not supplicate for him while his heart is heedless from him; rather, he should strive earnestly for him in the supplication.'

key_terms.قَلْبٍ: heart (in Islamic spirituality, the seat of intention and spiritual awareness)
key_terms.لَاهٍ: heedless, unmindful, distracted (the opposite of focused spiritual presence)
key_terms.لِيَجْتَهِدْ: let him strive, exert effort (from ijtihad — earnest application)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the condition of the heart during supplication?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) teaches that sincere, attentive presence of heart is an essential condition for the acceptance of du'a. This hadith addresses supplication on behalf of the deceased, warning that mere utterance of words without genuine focus and heartfelt engagement renders the prayer ineffective. In the context of early Islamic practice, supplicating for the dead after burial was a common act of piety; this teaching ensured that such prayers were performed with full mindfulness rather than as a rote ritual.
